text.p: - Debt-ridden shoe factory Peko, which stopped production on Tuesday, is expected to start operating today after it reached a deal on debt rescheduling with its leading creditor bank Gorenjska banka late Tuesday evening.
- The State Council (the upper house of parliament) confirmed a new law prohibiting advertising of tobacco products and trademarks that was passed by the lower house last week.
- Deputy secretary of the Italian Foreign Ministry Piero Fassino met representatives of Slovenian minorities in Italy on Tuesday, before starting a three-day visit to Slovenia.

- Slovenia and Croatia resumed talks after the summer break on mutual relations. One of the main issues under discussion is how to establish social security for citizens of both countries working across the border.
- Slovenian doctors' union Fides urged parliament to pass a law this week raising doctors' pay, before it is dissolved on Thursday ahead of the general election on November 10.
- A four-day international marketing fair "Golden Drum" started in Portoroz on Tuesday.

- Paper firm Videm Krsko is expected to stop production this week following a district court decision that the two firms renting Videm's production facilities must hand over the premises to Videm's new owner Czech holding ICEC.
- Officials from Slovenia, Italy and Hungary will meet in Maribor, Slovenia, on Wednesday to prepare for a meeting of their foreign ministers later this month or in November.
- Trading company Slovenijales hopes to overcome its financial problems following the appointment of new management last week. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
